note: What a community's values suggest for how it handles conflict and disputes. Up to 3 recommendations per value. All items need_review before use.

items.why: A formal hearing body makes responsibility explicit and creates a named record of what happened.
A standing committee adjudicating disputes creates consistent, named accountability across cases.
Dialogue-focused methods for understanding and repairing harm require all parties to own their impact.
Arbitrators chosen specifically for each case means the process adapts to the nature of the dispute.
A neutral facilitator helps guide the process, adapting it to what the situation actually requires.
A facilitator helps guide the process but parties drive the outcome themselves.
A neutral third party assists parties in reaching a voluntary agreement — parties decide, not the mediator.
Trained members mediate rather than authority figures — parties initiate without needing leadership permission.
Equal input from all involved resists hierarchies of who gets heard in dispute resolution.
